result:
I’m just gonna ramble about how weirdly beautiful the world is when you stop pretending it has to make sense.

Right now, outside my window, the sky is doing that obnoxious golden-hour thing where it looks like it’s been airbrushed by a Renaissance painter who got really into peach and lavender. A crow just landed on the power line, looked directly at me like we share a traumatic childhood, then flew off screaming what I’m choosing to interpret as “touch grass, nerd.” I respect the honesty.

I’ve been thinking lately about how most of our personalities are just scar tissue and coping mechanisms wearing a cute outfit. We’re all walking around with these elaborate origin stories we tell ourselves so the chaos feels narrated. “I’m not avoidant, I’m just mysterious and self-sufficient.” “I’m not addicted to my phone, I’m a digital anthropologist.” Meanwhile the crow is out there living in one continuous present tense, no lore, no playlist titled “songs that understand me,” just raw beak and attitude.

There’s something freeing about that. The older I get, the more I want to be more like the crow and less like a well-maintained brand. I want to scream at 7 a.m. for no reason other than the sun exists and I noticed. I want to collect shiny useless things (memories, weird rocks, people who laugh at the wrong jokes). I want to stop optimizing myself into irrelevance.

Life is absurd on purpose. The proof is that octopuses have three hearts and blue blood and can edit their own RNA like it’s a Google Doc, while I still can’t figure out how to fold a fitted sheet without wanting to fight God. The universe spent 13.8 billion years setting up this ridiculous Rube Goldberg machine that ends with me stress-eating cereal at 2 a.m. while listening to lo-fi beats and crying at an insurance commercial. That’s not a bug. That’s the entire point.

Anyway.

The peach light is gone now. The sky’s doing that bruised purple thing that makes everything feel like the last scene of a movie. The crow never came back. I hope he’s out there terrorizing someone else’s quiet evening with the sacred violence of just being alive.

I think I’m gonna go be unbearable for a while. In the best way possible.

Your turn. What’s the weirdest, most useless, most alive thing on your mind right now?
